answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, so creating thousands of sock puppets becomes expensive rather than free. Honest work slowly builds reputation, while misbehavior forfeits the stake, making a spiral of cheap new identities unprofitable. A newcomer starts with an ivory-clean record but no trust, and must earn standing gradually like a glacier moving, instead of instantly gaining full privileges.
